MOHAMAD KHALID Q. DIMAPORO Representative ISt District, Lanao del Norte House of Representatives Quezon City, Metro Manila Dear Representative Dimaporo: This refers to your electronic mail dated 2 August 2022 requesting for this Department's opinion conceming the erroneous utilization of the name of the duly elected Provincial Govemor in Lanao del Norte. Per your email, hereunder, quoted in verbatim, are the pertinent facts: "[Tlhe Provincial Govemment of Lanao del Norte has, for either political or personal reasons, been purposely utilizing an erroneous name of the duly elected Provincial Govemor. In the conduct of the 2022 National and Local Elections, candidate Imelda Quibranza-Dimaporo was elected into office as the Provincial Governor. The certificate of canvas and all other pertinent public documents that grant the electoral mandate to the position of Provincial Govemor is specifically named "Imelda Quibranza-Dimaporo". However, the Provincial Government is utilizing a different name in good conscious: "Imelda Dela Cruz Quibranza". This erroneous name may have been used in official communication letters and may be placed in sensitive official documents such as Provincial Govemment Checks, Notice of Awards, and Provincial Ordinances & Resolutions to name a few. Hence, the subject query. In addition thereto, it is requested for the Department "to elaborate on the plausible administrative penalties under the Department of the Interior and Local Govemment that may be charged to those involved should the practice of using an erroneous name on official documents be deemed improper. " At the outset, we shall take note of the correct name of the Govemor in our future correspondences. As to the query on the "plausible administrative penalties under the Department of the Interior and Local Govemment that may be charged to those involved should the practice of using an emoneous name on official documents be deemed improper", It is to be clarified that this Department is without authority to impose administrative Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

penalties to those involved in the practice of using an erroneous name of local govemment officials on official documents. Along this line, the Department does not act on concerns that are cognizable by other agencies of the govemment. At any rate, however, hereunder is a disquisition solely for academic purposes. Failure to use correct and proper names of public officials in official documents may subject the accountable official to neglect of duty. Relatedly, the Supreme Court in Civil Service Commission and the Office of the Solicitor General v. Catacutan [G.R. No. 224651, dated July 3, 2019] elucidated that: "The qravitv of negliqence or the character of neqlect in the performance of dutv is certainlv a matter of evidence and will direct the prooer sanction to be imposed. On one hand, gross neglect of duty is understood as the failure to give proper attention to a required task or to discharge a duty, characterized by want of even the slightest care, or by conscious indifference to the consequences insofar as other persons may be affected, or by flagrant and palpable breach of duty. It is the omission of that care which even inattentive and thoughtless men never fail to give to their own property. In cases involving public officials, there is gross negligence when a breach of duty is flagrant and palpable. Under the law, this offense warrants the supreme penalty of dismissal from service. Simple neglect of duty, on the other hand, is characterized by failure of an employee or official to give proper attention to a task expected of him or her, signifying a disregard of a duty resulting from carelessness or indifference. This warrants the penalty of mere suspension from office without pay." (Emphasis Supplied) Notwithstanding, we would like to reiterate that the opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same, and is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very respectfully yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MA Undersecr AN for Local Govemment OUSLG/ML1/LLLS-LRALLD/jam/c1p Dir. ARNEL M.
